originalTitle: Tata Steel Q1 net profit beats estimates; approves Rs 33,873 crore capex
simplifiedContent: Tata Steel, a big steel company, made more profit than expected in the first quarter of the year, with its profit increasing by about 12% compared to the same time last year. This happened mainly because the company did very well in the Indian market. The company also plans to spend a large amount of money, Rs 33,873 crore, to expand its businesses. Overall, the company's total revenue, or total amount of money made, increased by more than 14% in the quarter. This is important because it shows that the company is performing well, despite some challenges in its overseas operations.

originalTitle: Mahindra Q1 net profit rises 34%, standalone earnings beat estimates
simplifiedContent: Mahindra & Mahindra, a big company, just reported that it made 34% more profit in the first quarter of the year compared to last year. This is mainly because many people are buying their sport utility vehicles and tractors, which helped the company grow financially. However, the company had to spend more on materials, which affected its profit a little. The company's other businesses also did well and contributed to the good results. Despite some challenges, the company still thinks it will meet its financial goals for the whole year.

originalTitle: US stocks: Amazon beats estimates for quarterly cloud revenue growth
simplifiedContent: Amazon, a big US company, had a great quarter for its cloud business, which is like a big computer system that stores and processes lots of data. The company made more money from its cloud business than people thought it would, and this is because more big companies are using artificial intelligence (AI) technology. This is good news for Amazon and its investors. Other big companies like Microsoft and Google also had good results from their cloud businesses. Amazon's success in the cloud business is a sign that its investments in AI are paying off, which is a positive thing for the company.

originalTitle: Yen Surges as Nikkei Says Japan Intervened in Market Again
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen suddenly went up a lot against the US dollar, which is a big deal in the financial world. This happened because Japan's government stepped in to try and strengthen its own currency, according to a report from the Nikkei newspaper. The yen's value increased more in one day than it has in over two years. This matters because it can affect trade and investment between Japan and other countries, including the US. The government's action suggests they are trying to stabilize the yen's value, which could have further impacts on the economy.

originalTitle: Fitch’s Private Credit Default Rate Hit Record in Second Quarter
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Fitch Ratings, a company that keeps an eye on how well borrowers are paying back their debts, found that many private debt borrowers in the US are having trouble paying back their loans. In fact, the number of borrowers who couldn't pay back their loans, also known as the default rate, reached a record high in the second quarter. This means that out of the 1,300 borrowers that Fitch tracked, more of them defaulted on their loans than ever before. This matters because it shows that some borrowers are struggling financially, which could be a sign of trouble in the economy. It's worth paying attention to this news because it could affect the overall health of the financial market.

originalTitle: Yen soars as analysts suspect official intervention; dollar broadly weaker
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen has increased sharply, which means it can now buy more of other currencies than it could before. This happened because some experts think that the Japanese government or its central bank might be taking action to make the yen stronger. As a result, the US dollar has become weaker compared to other currencies. This matters because it can affect the prices of imported goods and the profits of companies that trade with other countries. The weaker dollar could also impact investors who have money in foreign stocks or bonds.
